newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller says rival will not get job.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller says rival will not get job.

text.p: Turkish conservative leader Tansu Ciller said on Friday she was confident that arch-rival Mesut Yilaz would not be appointed prime minister-designate in the search for a new coalition government.
"I don't think Mr Yilmaz will get it. There is no chance," Anatolian news agency quoted Foreign Minister Ciller as saying.
Yilmaz was due at the presidential palace later on Friday amid speculation that President Suleyman Demirel would nominate him to form a government.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, stepped down on June 18 under pressure from the secularist army.
He asked Demirel to appoint Ciller as the head of a new coalition with the Islamists that would take Turkey to early elections.
Ciller, on paper, has the support of 282 deputies in the 550-member assembly. Yilmaz has only 129 MPs and could struggle to find coalition allies.
